plan: In a second-price sealed-bid auction with independent private values, bidding one's true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do. This is because if I bid higher than my value, I risk winning and paying more than the item is worth to me; if I bid lower, I risk losing a profitable opportunity. Since I pay the second-highest bid (not my own bid) when I win, there's no incentive to shade my bid. Therefore, my optimal strategy is to bid exactly my value of $31, regardless of my beliefs about Betty and Charles's strategies.

In a second-price sealed-bid auction with independent private values, bidding one's true value is a weakly dominant strategy, regardless of other bidders' strategies or beliefs. This holds because: if I bid above value, I risk winning and paying more than the item is worth; if I bid below value, I risk losing profitable opportunities where the second-highest bid is between my true value and my bid. Since my value is $6, I will bid exactly $6, ensuring I only win when profitable and pay the appropriate second-highest bid.

In this second-price auction format, bidding your true value is the weakly dominant strategy regardless of what others do. My value for the item is $0, meaning winning would require paying more than $0 (unless I tie at $0), resulting in zero or negative profit. Therefore, the optimal bid is exactly my value: $0. This ensures I only "win" if the price is also $0, avoiding any loss.
